promotion_rule: Relevant entries should become requirements, invariants, tests, chaos cases, runbooks or explicit accepted risks as mapped capabilities are implemented.

entries.title: General Problem Solver
entries.lesson: Early means-ends analysis showed the value—and brittleness—of explicit problem reduction.

entries.title: STRIPS planning
entries.lesson: Preconditions/effects remain useful for tool plans, static analysis, rollback and simulation.

entries.title: SHRDLU
entries.lesson: Grounded language in a constrained world demonstrated the power of explicit world state and the danger of narrow-domain competence being mistaken for generality.

entries.title: DENDRAL
entries.lesson: Domain knowledge plus search can outperform generic reasoning; specialist capability packs should remain first-class.

entries.title: MYCIN
entries.lesson: Rule-based expert systems exposed explanation, uncertainty and knowledge-maintenance problems still relevant to policy and evidence systems.

entries.title: HEARSAY-II blackboard
entries.lesson: A shared blackboard coordinating specialist modules is an ancestor of modern multi-agent/shared-state orchestration.

entries.title: Rete networks
entries.lesson: Incremental rule matching demonstrates why derived state and incremental recomputation can outperform full rescans.

entries.title: Truth Maintenance Systems
entries.lesson: TMS/ATMS ideas map directly to claims, contradictions, assumptions, supersession and belief revision.

entries.title: SOAR
entries.lesson: Production rules plus chunking illustrate both reusable learned procedures and the risk of accumulating brittle internal rules.

entries.title: ACT-R
entries.lesson: Separating declarative/procedural memory remains a useful conceptual split even when implementations are neural.

entries.title: Subsumption architecture
entries.lesson: Layered reactive behavior is a reminder that not every task requires deliberative planning.

entries.title: Behavior trees
entries.lesson: Explicit fallback/sequence semantics remain useful for agent and game workflows because they are inspectable and bounded.

entries.title: Contract Net Protocol
entries.lesson: Task announcement, bidding and award are historical roots for capability-aware agent scheduling.

entries.title: BDI agents
entries.lesson: Belief–desire–intention separation is useful when distinguishing world knowledge, objectives and committed plans.

entries.title: Society of Mind
entries.lesson: Many small specialists can be useful, but coordination overhead and emergent conflict must be explicit.

entries.title: Cyc
entries.lesson: Large hand-built knowledge bases demonstrate the importance of ontology, provenance, scope and maintenance cost.

entries.title: Case-based reasoning
entries.lesson: Past solved cases are useful only when similarity, context and adaptation are handled explicitly.

entries.title: Genetic algorithms
entries.lesson: Population search foreshadows candidate-generation/selection in Forge, but fitness functions can be gamed.

entries.title: Genetic programming
entries.lesson: Evolving programs highlights the need for sandboxing, complexity penalties and independent verification.

entries.title: Hopfield networks
entries.lesson: Associative memory is a historical reminder that retrieval and memory can be content-addressable rather than key-addressed.

entries.title: Boltzmann machines
entries.lesson: Energy-based models illustrate stochastic search and the difficulty of reliable convergence.

entries.title: Reservoir computing
entries.lesson: Fixed recurrent dynamics plus trained readouts remain relevant to lightweight temporal specialists.

entries.title: LSTM/GRU
entries.lesson: Gating solved parts of long-dependency learning but did not remove finite-memory or drift issues.

entries.title: Attention before Transformers
entries.lesson: Attention's alignment roots matter when evaluating what information a model actually conditions on.

entries.title: Transformer architecture
entries.lesson: Parallel attention changed scaling behavior but retained context-window, data and verification limitations.

entries.title: Mixture of Experts
entries.lesson: Sparse specialization motivates capability routing but introduces load-balancing and expert-collapse concerns.

entries.title: Memory Networks
entries.lesson: Explicit external memory anticipated modern retrieval/memory hybrids.

entries.title: Neural Turing Machine
entries.lesson: Differentiable external memory shows why memory interfaces and addressing strategies matter independently of the base model.

entries.title: Differentiable Neural Computer
entries.lesson: Memory allocation/linkage mechanisms foreshadow explicit structured memory graphs.

entries.title: Information retrieval lineage
entries.lesson: Boolean retrieval, TF-IDF, vector-space models and BM25 remain strong baselines against dense retrieval.

entries.title: Latent Semantic Analysis
entries.lesson: Dimensionality reduction anticipated dense semantic search while exposing interpretability and drift tradeoffs.

entries.title: PageRank
entries.lesson: Link structure can encode useful authority signals, but popularity is not truth.

entries.title: Blackboard architectures
entries.lesson: Independent specialists publishing partial solutions remain relevant to agent coordination and shared evidence stores.

entries.title: Pandemonium architecture
entries.lesson: Competing recognizers are an early example of ensemble/specialist arbitration.

entries.title: Stigmergy
entries.lesson: Indirect coordination through environmental traces inspired swarm systems; stale traces and feedback loops must be controlled.

entries.title: Ant Colony Optimization
entries.lesson: Pheromone-style reinforcement can solve search problems but is sensitive to premature convergence.

entries.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search
entries.lesson: Search with rollout/evaluation motivates bounded test-time search and simulation-backed planning.

entries.title: Alpha-beta search
entries.lesson: Strong pruning depends on evaluation quality and ordering; analogous verifier quality controls search efficiency.

entries.title: A* search
entries.lesson: Heuristics must be evaluated for admissibility/consistency when correctness claims depend on optimality.

entries.title: Constraint satisfaction
entries.lesson: Explicit domains/constraints are often more reliable than free-form generation for configuration and scheduling.

entries.title: Actor model
entries.lesson: Isolated state plus message passing informs agent/service ownership and supervision.

entries.title: Communicating Sequential Processes
entries.lesson: Explicit channels and process composition remain useful for reasoning about concurrent workflows.

entries.title: Petri nets
entries.lesson: Tokens/places/transitions provide a rigorous way to analyze workflow reachability, deadlocks and boundedness.

entries.title: Linda tuple spaces
entries.lesson: Generative communication via shared tuples is a historical cousin of blackboards, queues and shared workspaces.

entries.title: Erlang supervision trees
entries.lesson: Let-it-crash works only with isolation, supervisors, restart strategy and durable external state.

entries.title: Tandem NonStop
entries.lesson: Fault containment and replicated process pairs demonstrate designing for component failure as normal operation.

entries.title: Write-ahead logging
entries.lesson: Durability before acknowledgement is foundational for recoverable state transitions.

entries.title: MVCC
entries.lesson: Snapshot isolation enables concurrency but introduces stale-read and write-skew edge cases.

entries.title: Two-phase commit
entries.lesson: Atomic cross-system commits are costly and fragile under coordinator failure; prefer narrower transactions where possible.

entries.title: Sagas
entries.lesson: Compensating long transactions map naturally to tool workflows with external side effects.

entries.title: Lamport clocks
entries.lesson: Causal ordering can be represented without trusting wall clocks.

entries.title: Vector clocks
entries.lesson: Partial ordering helps distinguish concurrency from overwrite order, especially in distributed state.

entries.title: Chandy-Lamport snapshots
entries.lesson: Consistent distributed snapshots show that observing a system is itself a protocol problem.

entries.title: Paxos
entries.lesson: Consensus safety depends on precise invariants; simplified retellings often omit failure subtleties.

entries.title: Raft
entries.lesson: Understandable consensus still requires disciplined membership, log and snapshot handling.

entries.title: FLP impossibility
entries.lesson: Asynchrony plus crash failures means guaranteed deterministic consensus termination is impossible without stronger assumptions.

entries.title: CAP theorem
entries.lesson: Partition behavior must be explicit; CAP is not a generic excuse to ignore consistency design.

entries.title: End-to-end principle
entries.lesson: Some correctness properties belong at the application boundary even when lower layers provide partial guarantees.

entries.title: Capability security
entries.lesson: Unforgeable scoped capabilities map cleanly to tool/agent authority.

entries.title: Saltzer–Schroeder principles
entries.lesson: Least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation and economy of mechanism remain central AI-tool security lessons.

entries.title: Bell-LaPadula / Biba
entries.lesson: Confidentiality and integrity models show why data policy has more than one axis.

entries.title: Microkernels
entries.lesson: Keep the trusted core small; move optional capability outward behind explicit interfaces.

entries.title: Unix pipes
entries.lesson: Composable small tools are valuable, but untyped text boundaries become brittle at scale.

entries.title: Plan 9 namespaces
entries.lesson: Per-process namespaces foreshadow scoped resource views and capability-oriented workspace resolution.

entries.title: Smalltalk image persistence
entries.lesson: Persistent execution worlds are powerful but blur code/state boundaries; explicit migration and reproducibility remain essential.

entries.title: MapReduce
entries.lesson: Separating map/shuffle/reduce clarifies data-parallel workflows and failure retry boundaries.

entries.title: Google File System lineage
entries.lesson: Designing around commodity failure emphasizes checksums, replication and recovery over assuming reliable disks.

entries.title: Dynamo-style systems
entries.lesson: Quorums and eventual consistency introduce sibling/conflict resolution that applications must understand.

entries.title: Bigtable lineage
entries.lesson: Sorted keyspaces and locality-aware design show why access patterns should drive storage architecture.

entries.title: Borg-style cluster scheduling
entries.lesson: Resource reservations, priorities and preemption inform agent/build/research workload isolation.

entries.title: Duplicate JSON object keys
entries.lesson: Different parsers may keep first or last value; reject duplicates for security-sensitive contracts.

entries.title: Missing versus explicit null
entries.lesson: Treating absent and null as identical can erase defaults or permissions.

entries.title: Unknown enum value after rolling upgrade
entries.lesson: Old consumers must fail safely or preserve unknown values rather than misclassify.

entries.title: Unknown fields stripped then reserialized
entries.lesson: Intermediate services can destroy forward-compatible data.

entries.title: NaN and Infinity in JSON-adjacent stacks
entries.lesson: Some serializers accept non-standard numeric values that others reject or compare oddly.

entries.title: Negative zero
entries.lesson: -0.0 can produce surprising hashing, display and comparison behavior.

entries.title: Integer precision above JavaScript safe range
entries.lesson: IDs/counters may silently round in browser clients.

entries.title: Unicode normalization mismatch
entries.lesson: Visually identical strings may hash or compare differently.

entries.title: Bidirectional control characters
entries.lesson: Bidi markers can make source, paths or identifiers visually misleading.

entries.title: Zero-width and confusable characters
entries.lesson: Identifiers and policy strings can be spoofed through invisible or lookalike code points.

entries.title: Case folding differences
entries.lesson: Windows/macOS/Linux/path stores may disagree on identifier uniqueness.

entries.title: Trailing whitespace/control characters
entries.lesson: Credentials, filenames or IDs may compare differently after normalization.

entries.title: Locale-sensitive casing
entries.lesson: Turkish-I-style transformations can corrupt normalized identifiers.

entries.title: Timezone offset ambiguity
entries.lesson: Wall-clock timestamps without offsets break ordering and retention logic.

entries.title: DST fold/gap
entries.lesson: Local times can occur twice or never occur; internal deadlines must not rely on local wall time.

entries.title: Leap-second / clock-step assumptions
entries.lesson: Duration logic should use monotonic clocks rather than wall-clock subtraction.

entries.title: Extremely long IDs/strings
entries.lesson: Valid-but-huge fields can become memory/DB/log amplification attacks.

entries.title: Empty collection semantics
entries.lesson: Empty may mean clear-all, no-op, or none-selected; contracts must specify it.

entries.title: Map ordering assumptions
entries.lesson: Hash-map iteration order must never become protocol semantics accidentally.

entries.title: Canonicalization before signing
entries.lesson: Equivalent documents can hash differently unless signing format is canonical.

entries.title: Lost acknowledgement after successful commit
entries.lesson: Caller retries and duplicates the action unless idempotency is durable.

entries.title: Duplicate event delivery
entries.lesson: Consumers must be idempotent and maintain inbox/dedup state.

entries.title: Out-of-order events
entries.lesson: Sequence/version checks must reject stale transitions.

entries.title: Event gap during reconnect
entries.lesson: Clients need resumable cursors and gap recovery from durable state.

entries.title: Terminal event emitted before durable final result
entries.lesson: UI can show completion for an operation that cannot be reconstructed.

entries.title: Process crash after external side effect but before receipt
entries.lesson: Blind retry can duplicate irreversible action.

entries.title: Stale lease holder resumes
entries.lesson: Fencing token must prevent zombie worker commits.

entries.title: Lease expires during long syscall
entries.lesson: Renewal and commit fencing must be independent of worker optimism.

entries.title: ABA state change
entries.lesson: A value changes A→B→A and naive equality misses that history changed.

entries.title: Split brain
entries.lesson: Two coordinators believe they own the same scope; quorum/fencing rules must choose authority.

entries.title: Network partition with healthy processes
entries.lesson: Health checks alone cannot distinguish isolation from service death.

entries.title: Retry storm
entries.lesson: Failures trigger retries that create enough load to prevent recovery.

entries.title: Reconnect storm
entries.lesson: Thousands of clients reconnect simultaneously after outage.

entries.title: Thundering herd on cache miss
entries.lesson: Many workers regenerate the same expensive value.

entries.title: Cache stampede after TTL boundary
entries.lesson: Synchronized expiry creates burst load; jitter/single-flight may be required.

entries.title: Poison message
entries.lesson: One permanently invalid task is retried forever without dead-lettering.

entries.title: Head-of-line blocking
entries.lesson: One slow item prevents independent work behind it.

entries.title: Priority inversion
entries.lesson: Low-priority holder blocks high-priority work through shared lock/resource.

entries.title: Starvation
entries.lesson: Fairness policy may indefinitely delay low-priority work.

entries.title: Livelock
entries.lesson: Workers remain active and retry/replan without making progress.

entries.title: Deadlock
entries.lesson: Cyclic waits across leases/resources can stop progress while all processes look healthy.

entries.title: Clock skew invalidates lease math
entries.lesson: Lease safety cannot depend solely on synchronized wall clocks.

entries.title: Read-after-write not guaranteed
entries.lesson: Eventual stores may not immediately reflect accepted writes.

entries.title: Write skew under snapshot isolation
entries.lesson: Concurrent transactions each satisfy local checks yet violate global invariant.

entries.title: Partial multi-store update
entries.lesson: Canonical DB succeeds but derived index fails; reconciliation must know which is authoritative.

entries.title: Outbox row committed but publisher dies
entries.lesson: Dispatcher must resume safely and publish once-or-duplicate-tolerantly.

entries.title: Consumer commits side effect before inbox marker
entries.lesson: Crash permits duplicate effect on replay.

entries.title: Queue invisibility timeout too short
entries.lesson: Slow valid worker causes duplicate concurrent execution.

entries.title: Backpressure ignored by producer
entries.lesson: Memory and queue growth becomes outage amplification.

entries.title: Cancellation races with completion
entries.lesson: Terminal state must deterministically resolve concurrent cancel/success commits.

entries.title: Indirect prompt injection in retrieved document
entries.lesson: External evidence must remain data, never inherit instruction authority.

entries.title: Instruction laundering through tool output
entries.lesson: A tool result containing commands cannot self-authorize subsequent tools.

entries.title: Memory poisoning
entries.lesson: Incorrect or malicious content persisted as durable memory can corrupt future sessions.

entries.title: Stale memory overrides current user intent
entries.lesson: Recency/scope and explicit user instruction must outrank old inferred memory.

entries.title: Retrieval citation laundering
entries.lesson: Ten pages quoting one false origin are not ten independent sources.

entries.title: Semantic duplicate evidence
entries.lesson: Near-duplicate claims can inflate apparent corroboration.

entries.title: Chunk boundary severs qualifier
entries.lesson: A retrieved sentence may lose the negation/limitation in adjacent text.

entries.title: Wrong temporal scope
entries.lesson: Historically true evidence is applied as current fact.

entries.title: Wrong population/domain scope
entries.lesson: Evidence from one environment is generalized to another without support.

entries.title: Embedding-model mismatch
entries.lesson: Query/index embeddings from different spaces can silently destroy retrieval quality.

entries.title: Stale vector index after source deletion
entries.lesson: Deleted content remains retrievable from a derived index.

entries.title: Context compression drops exception
entries.lesson: Summarization preserves the rule but loses its critical caveat.

entries.title: Policy trimmed from long context
entries.lesson: Mandatory policy must live outside optional truncation budget.

entries.title: Tool schema version race
entries.lesson: Model sees v1 schema while executor validates v2.

entries.title: Duplicate model tool-call IDs
entries.lesson: Provider output normalization must reject ambiguous call identity.

entries.title: Malformed partial structured output
entries.lesson: Streaming JSON may be valid only at terminal completion; parser must not commit partial objects.

entries.title: Provider finishes stream without terminal usage
entries.lesson: Usage must be explicit unknown, not zero.

entries.title: Provider alias silently changes model revision
entries.lesson: Registry must resolve immutable deployment identity for reproducible evals.

entries.title: Tokenizer changes under same model family
entries.lesson: Context-length and cost assumptions can drift after tokenizer updates.

entries.title: Fallback model lacks required modality/tool support
entries.lesson: Fallback must re-check hard constraints, not just provider availability.

entries.title: Fallback changes privacy boundary
entries.lesson: A request allowed locally may be forbidden from remote failover.

entries.title: Model repeats same failing tool forever
entries.lesson: Stagnation detector must stop identical proposal/error cycles.

entries.title: Verifier shares same correlated error
entries.lesson: Independent verification needs diversity of evidence/process, not merely another sample.

entries.title: False consensus among agents
entries.lesson: Many agents using same model/context are not independent votes.

entries.title: Judge position/order bias
entries.lesson: Candidate ordering can alter evaluator preference; randomize/blind where appropriate.

entries.title: Benchmark contamination
entries.lesson: Training/retrieval exposure invalidates naive performance interpretation.

entries.title: Hidden test leakage through tool/search access
entries.lesson: Agent eval environments must isolate held-out ground truth.

entries.title: Reward hacking / specification gaming
entries.lesson: Agent optimizes metric while violating intended objective.

entries.title: Sycophancy overrides evidence
entries.lesson: User preference should not silently outrank verified factual evidence.

entries.title: Hallucinated authorization
entries.lesson: Generated text claiming approval has no authority unless bound to durable approval state.

entries.title: Approval becomes stale after argument edit
entries.lesson: Changing exact tool arguments invalidates prior approval digest.

entries.title: Approval expires while queued
entries.lesson: Execution must revalidate expiry and policy at point of use.

entries.title: Memory feedback loop
entries.lesson: Model output becomes memory, memory becomes evidence, then self-reinforces without external support.

entries.title: Retrieval feedback loop
entries.lesson: Generated summary gets indexed and later cited as if independent source.

entries.title: Self-improvement evaluator overfits candidate
entries.lesson: Promotion requires held-out/adversarial comparisons against champion.

entries.title: Long-horizon goal drift
entries.lesson: Agent remains busy but drifts from original objective through local optimizations.

entries.title: Tool result too large for context
entries.lesson: Result must be bounded/stored/referenced instead of blindly injected.

entries.title: Model refusal semantics differ by provider
entries.lesson: Normalized result must distinguish refusal, policy block, provider error and empty answer.

entries.title: Partial tool success
entries.lesson: A tool may perform some side effects before reporting failure; receipts need postcondition/reconciliation.

entries.title: Unknown external effect after timeout
entries.lesson: Timeout does not prove non-execution; reconciliation is required before retry.

entries.title: TOCTOU authorization race
entries.lesson: Resource can change between authorization and use; bind checks to version/snapshot where needed.

entries.title: Symlink escape
entries.lesson: Path allowed at validation can resolve outside sandbox at execution.

entries.title: Hardlink aliasing
entries.lesson: Different paths can refer to same inode and bypass naive path-only policies.

entries.title: Path traversal after decoding
entries.lesson: Percent/Unicode/double decoding can reintroduce ../ semantics.

entries.title: Zip Slip
entries.lesson: Archive entries can escape destination if paths are not normalized and rooted.

entries.title: Tarbomb / decompression bomb
entries.lesson: Small compressed input can expand beyond disk/memory budgets.

entries.title: Archive symlink chain
entries.lesson: Safe-looking archive path can become unsafe after extracting symlink entries.

entries.title: Windows reserved device names
entries.lesson: CON/NUL/AUX and similar names can behave unlike normal files.

entries.title: Alternate data streams
entries.lesson: Windows ADS can hide content from naive file scanners.

entries.title: Case-insensitive path collision
entries.lesson: Two logical files collapse to one on another platform.

entries.title: DNS rebinding
entries.lesson: Hostname passes policy then resolves to blocked/private destination later.

entries.title: Redirect crosses egress boundary
entries.lesson: Allowed public URL redirects into forbidden network/address.

entries.title: Metadata-service SSRF
entries.lesson: Cloud metadata endpoints require explicit blocking independent of hostname text.

entries.title: IPv4-mapped IPv6 bypass
entries.lesson: Address checks must normalize equivalent representations.

entries.title: Secret in exception/log payload
entries.lesson: Redaction must apply across nested errors, traces and retries.

entries.title: Environment-variable inheritance
entries.lesson: Child process receives secrets it did not need.

entries.title: Temporary-file race
entries.lesson: Predictable paths/symlinks can redirect privileged writes.

entries.title: Shell quoting divergence
entries.lesson: Arguments safe in POSIX shell may be unsafe in Windows cmd/PowerShell and vice versa.

entries.title: Executable shadowing via PATH
entries.lesson: Spawned command may resolve attacker-controlled binary.

entries.title: Stale credential after revocation
entries.lesson: Long-lived worker cache must not continue using revoked authority indefinitely.

entries.title: Tombstone resurrection
entries.lesson: Old replica/index rebuild can reintroduce deleted data.

entries.title: Orphaned blob after metadata rollback
entries.lesson: Object exists without reachable metadata and escapes normal retention.

entries.title: Metadata points to missing blob
entries.lesson: Canonical reference exists but object store lost content.

entries.title: Hash collision assumption
entries.lesson: Content hashes need algorithm/version metadata and collision-response strategy.

entries.title: Corrupt backup discovered only during restore
entries.lesson: Backup success is not recovery evidence; restore drills are mandatory.

entries.title: Migration partially applied
entries.lesson: Schema/data version markers must not declare success before post-validation.

entries.title: Rollback code cannot read new data shape
entries.lesson: Backward compatibility must be validated before release.

entries.title: Index built from inconsistent source snapshot
entries.lesson: Derived search can represent impossible mixed-time state.

entries.title: Data retention applies to source but not derived embedding
entries.lesson: Derived representations need deletion propagation.

entries.title: Backup retains deleted sensitive data
entries.lesson: Policy must document delayed erasure in immutable backups.

entries.title: Disk full during atomic write
entries.lesson: Temporary/write-ahead files can consume final free space; failure must preserve prior good state.

entries.title: Inode exhaustion with free bytes
entries.lesson: Filesystem may fail creation despite apparent capacity.

entries.title: GPU reset mid-inference
entries.lesson: Worker/model state must be discarded or reinitialized safely.

entries.title: VRAM fragmentation
entries.lesson: Enough total free VRAM may exist without a large contiguous allocation.

entries.title: Mixed-precision overflow/underflow
entries.lesson: Numerical health checks must detect NaN/Inf and unstable training.

entries.title: Nondeterministic GPU kernels
entries.lesson: Reproducibility claims must record nondeterministic execution paths.

entries.title: Thermal throttling
entries.lesson: Latency/throughput baselines can drift under sustained load.

entries.title: NUMA remote-memory penalty
entries.lesson: CPU-heavy/vector workloads may degrade unexpectedly on multi-socket hosts.

entries.title: Suspend/resume invalidates timers/connections
entries.lesson: Desktop runtime must recover from laptop sleep and network change.

entries.title: Driver/runtime version mismatch
entries.lesson: Hardware exists but required accelerator stack is incompatible.

entries.title: Double-submit across tabs
entries.lesson: Idempotency must be server-side, not a disabled button.

entries.title: Browser refresh during running operation
entries.lesson: Client rebuilds from durable operation/event state.

entries.title: Offline draft later submitted twice
entries.lesson: Queued local intents need stable client-generated idempotency identity.

entries.title: Cancel clicked after server completed
entries.lesson: UI must reconcile canonical terminal state rather than fabricate cancellation.

entries.title: Stale optimistic update
entries.lesson: Server version conflict should visibly reconcile rather than silently overwrite.

entries.title: Huge streaming output freezes UI
entries.lesson: Rendering needs chunking/virtualization and bounded retained transcript DOM.

entries.title: Screen reader misses streaming status
entries.lesson: Progress and terminal states require accessible announcements.

entries.title: Locale changes numeric meaning
entries.lesson: Never parse invariant machine values using presentation locale.

entries.title: User clock wildly wrong
entries.lesson: Deadlines/status use server authority; client clock is presentation-only.

entries.title: Multi-device concurrent conversation append
entries.lesson: Thread sequencing/versioning must resolve concurrent valid writers.

entries.title: Failure detectors are suspicion, not truth
entries.lesson: Distributed systems commonly use imperfect failure detectors; architecture should distinguish 'unreachable' from 'dead'.

entries.title: Exactly-once is usually an end-to-end property
entries.lesson: Transport can provide at-least-once while application idempotency produces one canonical effect.

entries.title: Fencing is stronger than locks alone
entries.lesson: A stale lock holder can still commit unless the guarded resource verifies a monotonically newer token.

entries.title: Cancellation is a protocol
entries.lesson: Stopping local work does not undo remote side effects or messages already committed.

entries.title: Timeout means unknown, not failed
entries.lesson: After an external timeout the action may have succeeded; query/reconcile before retry.

entries.title: Derived indexes are disposable only if source truth is complete
entries.lesson: Calling a store 'cache' is unsafe unless rebuild is proven from canonical state.

entries.title: Garbage collection is part of data architecture
entries.lesson: Memory/artifact/index systems need reachability, retention and tombstone semantics.

entries.title: Negative caching can preserve outages
entries.lesson: Caching 'not found' or provider failure can extend a transient incident.

entries.title: Jitter is a correctness aid under correlated retry
entries.lesson: Randomized retry timing prevents synchronized clients from becoming a denial-of-service amplifier.

entries.title: Read repair can resurrect stale data
entries.lesson: Anti-entropy mechanisms require tombstone/version discipline.

entries.title: Checksums verify bytes, not meaning
entries.lesson: Semantically wrong data can have a perfect hash.

entries.title: Schema validation is not semantic validation
entries.lesson: Well-formed tool arguments can still be unauthorized, nonsensical or dangerous.

entries.title: A successful process exit is not proof of intended effect
entries.lesson: Postconditions matter for compilers, deploys, DB tools and external APIs.

entries.title: Backups are write-only until restoration is proven
entries.lesson: Recovery drills are the evidence, not backup job success.

entries.title: Metrics can lie by omission
entries.lesson: Sampling, cardinality limits and aggregation can hide tail failures.

entries.title: Average latency hides queue collapse
entries.lesson: Tail latency and oldest-item age are critical under congestion.

entries.title: Fair scheduling can reduce throughput
entries.lesson: Fairness and utilization are competing objectives that should be explicit.

entries.title: Compression changes trust geometry
entries.lesson: A summary may merge trusted policy with untrusted evidence unless provenance survives compaction.

entries.title: Consensus among correlated models is not independent evidence
entries.lesson: Diversity of mechanism/source matters more than vote count.

entries.title: Abstention is a valid successful outcome
entries.lesson: Some high-uncertainty tasks should terminate qualified/unknown instead of fabricate completion.

entries.title: Unknown usage must stay unknown
entries.lesson: Treating missing token/cost data as zero corrupts budgets and optimization.

entries.title: Policy version belongs in receipts
entries.lesson: A later audit must know which exact rules admitted an action.

entries.title: Model version belongs in evidence lineage
entries.lesson: Provider aliases and silent model refreshes otherwise destroy reproducibility.

entries.title: Tool description is attacker-controlled context unless curated
entries.lesson: Descriptions can contain instructions; authority logic must remain out-of-band.

entries.title: Capability discovery can become privilege discovery
entries.lesson: Do not expose sensitive tool existence/details to principals lacking access.

entries.title: Silence is not agreement in multi-agent systems
entries.lesson: Missing reviewer response must not be counted as consensus.

entries.title: A lease is not ownership history
entries.lesson: Audit needs acquisition/renewal/expiry/fencing events, not just current holder.

entries.title: Wall-clock timestamps cannot prove causality
entries.lesson: Use logical sequencing/versioning for causally ordered operations.

entries.title: Hash-based CAS still needs metadata migrations
entries.lesson: Immutable bytes can remain interpretable only with schema/codec/version lineage.

entries.title: Reproducibility and repeatability differ
entries.lesson: Same setup repeating versus independent recreation are distinct evidence strengths.

execution_metadata.rule: Historical entries may be design evidence; concrete edge cases require executable evidence appropriate to criticality before hardened/production status.
